pages.title: The Settings and Data menus
pages.description: Every control in Settings and in the Data menu, the guide window, the Claude connection and the version chip.
pages.intro: Settings is in the window bar at the top right, on every tab. The Data menu is under the tabs, on the right. Each picture names its controls. Point at a number, on the picture or in the list, to find it.

views.text: Five parts, top to bottom. Click outside the menu, or press Esc, to close it.

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: Opens and closes this menu.

marks.label: Display
marks.text: App scale: makes the whole app bigger or smaller.

marks.label: Portfolio targets
marks.text: The DSCR, LTV and debt-yield targets the Portfolio page measures against.

marks.label: Portfolio
marks.text: How many properties there are, each one by name, and any that look like duplicates.

marks.label: Open the guide
marks.text: Opens this guide (see below).

marks.label: Cloud
marks.text: The Claude connection for the AI features.

views.title: App scale
views.text: Everything below the window bar grows or shrinks at once, like zoom in a web browser. The window bar keeps its size, so Settings is always easy to reach. The app starts at 100% each time you open it.

marks.label: Size now
marks.text: The size the app is at.

marks.label: Slider
marks.text: From 50% to 200%, in steps of 5%.
Half size: the most fits on the screen.
Normal size (lit when it is the size now).
Double size. 75%, 125% and 150% are in between.

marks.label: Reset to 100%
marks.text: Back to the normal size.

views.title: Portfolio targets
views.text: What the Portfolio page measures against: its tiles, the Coverage vs targets chart and the coverage table (clears / off target). Type a figure and click away, or press Tab. See [Set the portfolio targets](set-portfolio-targets).

marks.label: Minimum DSCR
marks.text: NOI ÷ yearly loan payments should be at least this (1.25× to start).

marks.label: Maximum LTV
marks.text: Balance ÷ value should be at most this (75% to start).

marks.label: Minimum debt yield
marks.text: NOI ÷ balance should be at least this (8% to start).

marks.label: Where they are used
marks.text: Only on the Portfolio page. The refinance’s “Can you?” limits are fixed; Underwriting sets its sizing limits for each property.

views.title: Your properties
views.text: How many properties the app counts, each one listed by name, so you can check the count against your own list. Below the list, any two properties that may be one building: the same street address, or similar names where one has no address. Here two made-up properties, “Sample Court” and “Sample Court East”, are flagged.

marks.label: Properties
marks.text: How many properties there are; under it, how many loans they hold.

marks.label: Every property
marks.text: Numbered, with the start of each one’s address. Scroll it to see them all.

marks.label: Possible duplicate
marks.text: The two names, and why they were flagged.

marks.label: Not a duplicate
marks.text: They really are two buildings: the pair isn’t flagged again.

marks.label: If they are one building
marks.text: Rename one to match the other (on its property page) and they become one property.

views.title: After “Not a duplicate”
views.text: The app remembers the pair. Data Health shows the same check.

marks.label: No duplicates
marks.text: Nothing left to look at.

sections.title: The guide
sections.text: **Open the guide** in Settings opens this guide in a window over the app, on its Overview. Esc or **×** closes it.

views.title: A page
views.text: The pages are on the left, in groups. A how-to page gets one task done, step by step; a reference page names every control on a screen.

marks.label: Guide
marks.text: Back to the Overview.

marks.label: Search the guide
marks.text: Finds every page, section and step with all the words you type. Ctrl K jumps here.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the guide (so does Esc).

marks.label: The pages
marks.text: Every page, in its group. The page you are reading is lit.

marks.label: The page
marks.text: Its title, what it gets done, and what you need first.

marks.label: On this page
marks.text: The page’s sections. Click one to jump to it; the one you are reading is lit.

views.title: Steps and pictures
views.text: Each step is one action. A picture shows the app where the screen changes, with numbers on what the step points at. At the foot of each page, **Next steps** and **Previous** / **Next** lead on.

marks.label: A step
marks.text: What to do, and what happens then.

marks.label: The picture
marks.text: The app itself. Click it to see it full size; click again, or press Esc, to go back.

marks.label: A number
marks.text: Point at it, or at its line in the list, and both light up with the part of the screen it marks.

marks.label: What each number is
marks.text: The same numbers, in words. With more than three, the list sits beside the picture on a wide window.

views.title: Search
views.text: Every page, section and step that has all the words you typed, with where it is. Click one to go there; Enter opens the first.

marks.label: Search
marks.text: What you typed.

marks.label: Results
marks.text: How many places match.

marks.label: A result
marks.text: Its group, page and section, and its first words. Click to go there.

sections.title: Claude connection
sections.text: Opened by **Claude connection** at the foot of Settings. See [Connect Claude](connect-claude).

views.title: Connected
views.text: The top line says whether the app can reach Claude, and how. Here it is signed in with a Claude subscription. Close the window with **×** or by clicking outside it.

marks.label: Claude connection
marks.text: Your Claude subscription or an API key.

marks.label: Close
marks.text: Closes the window.

marks.label: State
marks.text: Green: connected, and how. Amber: not connected, and what to do.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Disconnects your Claude subscription on this computer.

marks.label: Advanced
marks.text: Use an Anthropic API key instead.

views.title: Advanced — an API key
views.text: For pay-as-you-go use at console.anthropic.com instead of a subscription. Once a key is saved, **Clear** appears beside **Save** and removes it.

marks.label: Advanced
marks.text: Opens and closes this part.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Paste the key here (it starts sk-ant-). It is hidden as you type.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves the key and switches the app to use it.

marks.label: Where it is kept
marks.text: Only on this computer.

views.title: Not connected
views.text: Before you connect, or after **Sign out**. The line at the top turns amber and says what is missing.

marks.label: Not connected
marks.text: Says what is missing.

marks.label: Connect with your Claude subscription
marks.text: Opens a small sign-in window that takes you to your browser.

marks.label: How it works
marks.text: What happens when you click it.

sections.title: The Data menu
sections.text: The **Data** button is under the tabs, on the right, on both sides of the **Whole Portfolio** / **Specific Property** switch.

views.text: Backups of everything, and loans in and out of Excel. Below them, the backups the app takes by itself.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Opens and closes this menu.

marks.label: Back up to a file…
marks.text: Saves everything to one file you choose: every loan, every property’s folder (profile, assumptions, T12s, documents), every chat and your settings.

marks.label: Restore from a file…
marks.text: Replaces everything with a backup file you pick. It asks first, and saves what you have as an automatic backup.

marks.label: Export all loans to Excel…
marks.text: A workbook of every active loan.

marks.label: Import loans from Excel…
marks.text: Adds or updates loans from a workbook.

marks.label: An automatic backup
marks.text: Why it was taken (“After: Added property …”, “After a change”, “Before Excel import”, “Before a restore”), when, and what it holds. Click to restore it.

marks.label: Open folder
marks.text: Opens the folder with the automatic backups on your computer.

views.title: Restoring a backup
views.text: Before a restore, the app says exactly what the backup holds and what it replaces. **Restore** replaces your loans, property folders and chats, then the app reloads with the restored data.

marks.label: Restore …?
marks.text: What the backup holds.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: What is replaced, and that your current data is saved first, as a “Before a restore” backup.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Restores the backup.

views.text: Exactly what the workbook will hold: one column per active loan, one row per field, in sections. The values can’t be edited here. Removed, paid-off and archived loans aren’t exported.

marks.label: Export to Excel
marks.text: A preview of the workbook.

marks.label: How many
marks.text: How many loans will be exported.

marks.label: Field
marks.text: Each row is one field of a loan, grouped in sections (the green bands).

marks.label: A loan
marks.text: Untick to leave this loan out.

marks.label: Select all
marks.text: Ticks or unticks every loan.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without exporting.

marks.label: Export
marks.text: Saves the workbook (your computer’s Save window opens).

views.title: Before you import
views.text: The details every loan in your sheet needs. Loans can be in rows or in columns, and small differences in the headers are fine; an export from the app always works.

marks.label: Before you import
marks.text: What your sheet needs.

marks.label: The details
marks.text: Every detail a loan needs.

marks.label: I’ve checked
marks.text: Tick it to turn on Choose file…

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes without importing.

marks.label: Choose file…
marks.text: Opens your computer’s Open window to pick the workbook.

views.title: Review import
views.text: Nothing has changed yet. Each loan in the workbook is a row with its status, and you can edit any cell. This made-up workbook holds an export of two sample loans (one with a changed insurance escrow) and two made-up loans, one of them incomplete.

marks.label: Review import
marks.text: What the workbook would do.

marks.label: Counts
marks.text: New, updated, unchanged, and how many need attention.

marks.label: unchanged
marks.text: Matches a loan you have; nothing differs.

marks.label: update
marks.text: Matches a loan you have; the changed details will be written to it (only the details the sheet has).

marks.label: new
marks.text: No match: it will be added.

marks.label: missing data
marks.text: Needs a detail the sheet didn’t have.

marks.label: + Add loan
marks.text: Adds an empty row to fill in.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Closes; nothing is imported.

marks.label: Resolve 1 to import
marks.text: Turns into **Apply import** once nothing needs attention. Apply saves an automatic backup first.

views.text: At the right of the header, under the window bar. See [Update the app](update-the-app).

marks.label: Property count
marks.text: How many properties are in the portfolio.

marks.label: Version
marks.text: Your version. Click to check for an update: “Checking for updates…”, then “Update available…” and “Downloading update… %”. Green “Update ready — Restart” means one is downloaded; click it to restart into it.

pages.title: Connect Claude
pages.description: Turn on the AI features with your Claude subscription, or with an Anthropic API key.
pages.intro: Claude reads each T12 a second time, writes the stories and What to push, and answers in the assistant. Connect it once on this computer. Your Claude subscription is the recommended way: nothing to install and nothing billed per use. An Anthropic API key is the other way, paid as you go.
before: A Claude Pro or Max subscription, or an Anthropic API key from console.anthropic.com.

steps.text: Click **Settings** at the top right of the window. At the foot of the menu, **Claude connection** says **Connected** or **Not set**.

marks.label: Settings
marks.text: Opens the menu.

marks.label: Claude connection
marks.text: Opens the connection window.

marks.label: Not set
marks.text: Claude isn’t connected yet.

steps.text: Click **Claude connection**. Its window says what is missing.

marks.label: Not connected
marks.text: Amber, with what is missing.

marks.label: Connect with your Claude subscription
marks.text: Click it next.

steps.text: Click **Connect with your Claude subscription**. A small sign-in window opens and takes you to your browser.
Sign in to your Claude subscription in the browser. Close the small window once it says you are signed in.
Back in **Claude connection**, the line at the top turns green: **Connected · signed in to your Claude subscription**.

marks.label: Connected
marks.text: The AI features are on.

marks.label: Sign out
marks.text: Disconnects the subscription on this computer.

callouts.text: The assistant has the same choices under **Connection settings**, and shows them by itself when Claude isn’t connected.

sections.title: Use an API key instead
sections.text: Without a subscription, use a key from console.anthropic.com and pay as you go.

steps.text: In **Claude connection**, click **Advanced — use an Anthropic API key instead**.
Paste your key in **Anthropic API key**. It starts with sk-ant- and is hidden as you type.

marks.label: Anthropic API key
marks.text: Your key, hidden.

marks.label: Save
marks.text: Saves it and switches the app to it.

steps.text: Click **Save**. The key is kept only on this computer, and the top line reads **Connected · using your Anthropic API key**.

marks.label: Connected
marks.text: Through your API key.

marks.label: Clear
marks.text: Removes the key from this computer. The app goes back to your subscription when it is signed in.

callouts.text: A saved key is used for every AI feature, even with a subscription signed in. To go back to the subscription, click **Clear**, or pick **Automatic (recommended)** or **Claude subscription** in the assistant’s **Connection settings**.

next.text: Every control in the connection window.

pages.title: Set the portfolio targets
pages.description: Choose the DSCR, LTV and debt yield the Portfolio page measures every property against.
pages.intro: The Portfolio page holds each property to three targets: a minimum DSCR, a maximum LTV and a minimum debt yield. Its tiles, the Coverage vs targets chart and the coverage table all follow them. Set them to your own standard.

steps.text: Click **Settings** at the top right of the window.
Under **Portfolio targets (Home)**, type a new figure in **Minimum DSCR (target)**, **Maximum LTV (target)** or **Minimum debt yield (target)**.

marks.label: Minimum DSCR
marks.text: 1.25× to start.

marks.label: Maximum LTV
marks.text: 75% to start.

marks.label: Minimum debt yield
marks.text: 8% to start.

steps.text: Click away, or press Tab. The Portfolio page measures every property against the new figure at once, and the targets are kept for next time.

callouts.text: These targets are only for the Portfolio page. The refinance’s “Can you?” limits are fixed, and Underwriting sets its own sizing limits for each property.

next.text: See each property against the targets.
Underwriting’s own limits, property by property.

pages.title: Back up and restore
pages.description: Save everything to one file, and put it back from a file or from an automatic backup.
pages.intro: A backup is one file with everything: every loan, every property’s folder (profile, assumptions, T12s, documents), every chat and your settings. Restore it on this computer or another one. The app also keeps backups by itself, a few seconds after a change and before an Excel import or a restore.

callouts.text: A restore replaces your loans, every property folder and every chat. What you have just before it is saved first, as a **Before a restore** backup, so you can switch back.

steps.text: Click **Data**, under the tabs on the right.

marks.label: Data
marks.text: Opens the menu.

marks.label: Back up to a file…
marks.text: Saves everything to one file.

marks.label: Restore from a file…
marks.text: Puts a backup file back.

steps.text: Click **Back up to a file…**. Your computer’s Save window opens.
Pick a folder and click **Save**. The app says what it backed up.
Click **Data**, then **Restore from a file…**. Your computer’s Open window opens.
Pick the backup file. The app says what is in it and what it will replace.
Click **Restore**. The app reloads with the restored data.
Click **Data**. Under **Recent automatic backups**, each line says why it was taken, when, and what it holds.

marks.label: An automatic backup
marks.text: Why it was taken, when, and what it holds. The newest is first.

marks.label: Open folder
marks.text: The folder that holds them on your computer.

steps.text: Click the backup you want. The app says what it holds and what it will replace.

marks.label: What happens
marks.text: What is replaced, and that your data now is saved first.

marks.label: Restore
marks.text: Restores the backup.

marks.label: Cancel
marks.text: Nothing changes.

steps.text: Click **Restore**. The app reloads with the restored data.

next.text: Move loans in and out of Excel.
Upload a backup file as a shared group’s starting data.

pages.title: Move loans in and out of Excel
pages.description: Export your loans to a workbook, or add and update loans from one.
pages.intro: Export puts every active loan in an Excel workbook, one column per loan. Import reads a workbook and adds the new loans and updates the ones you already have. Nothing changes until you have reviewed the import and applied it.

steps.text: Click **Data**, then **Export all loans to Excel…**. A preview shows exactly what the workbook will hold.

marks.label: A loan
marks.text: One column per loan. Untick to leave it out.

marks.label: Select all
marks.text: Ticks or unticks every loan.

marks.label: Export
marks.text: Saves the workbook.

steps.text: Untick any loan you want to leave out.
Click **Export**, then save the .xlsx file in your computer’s Save window.

callouts.text: Removed, paid-off and archived loans aren’t exported. The preview can’t be edited: change a loan in the app.

steps.text: Click **Data**, then **Import loans from Excel…**. A list names the details each loan in your sheet needs.

marks.label: The details
marks.text: What each loan needs.

marks.label: I’ve checked
marks.text: Tick it to turn on Choose file…

marks.label: Choose file…
marks.text: Opens your computer’s Open window.

steps.text: Tick **I’ve checked my sheet includes these details**, then click **Choose file…** and pick the workbook.
Check each row’s status: **new** (it will be added), **update** (it matches a loan you have, and something differs), **unchanged**, or **missing data**. Nothing has changed yet.

marks.label: Counts
marks.text: How many of each, and how many need attention.

marks.label: missing data
marks.text: A required detail the sheet didn’t have.

steps.text: Type the missing detail in each amber cell, or click **✕** at the end of its row to leave that loan out. Here the incomplete made-up loan is removed.

marks.label: Ready
marks.text: 1 new, 1 updated, 1 unchanged: nothing needs attention.
Removes that row from the import.

marks.label: Apply import (2)
marks.text: Imports the new and the updated loans.

steps.text: Click **Apply import**. The app saves an automatic backup, adds the new loans and writes the changes to the updated ones. Unchanged loans stay exactly as they are.

callouts.text: An export from the app always imports. Loans can be in rows or in columns, and small differences in the headers are fine.

steps.text: Click **Data**. The backup taken just before the import is listed in amber as **Before Excel import**.

marks.label: Before Excel import
marks.text: Taken just before the import.

marks.label: After …
marks.text: Taken a few seconds after a change, naming it: here the import.

steps.text: Click **Before Excel import**, then **Restore**. Everything goes back to how it was just before the import.

next.text: Back up everything, and restore it.
Change a loan in the app.
Every control in the export and the import.

pages.title: Update the app
pages.description: Check for a new version, and restart into it.
pages.intro: The chip at the right of the header shows the version you have. Click it to check for a new one: the app downloads it by itself, then asks you to restart.

steps.text: Click the version chip at the right of the header (it shows your version). It reads **Checking for updates…**.

marks.label: Version
marks.text: The version you have. Click it to check.

steps.text: If there is a new version, the chip reads **Update available…**, then **Downloading update…** with how far it is. If you are up to date, the app says so.
When the chip turns green and reads **Update ready — Restart**, click it. The app restarts into the new version.

callouts.text: Updates never touch your loans, files, chats or backups.

next.text: The version chip and the header.
